claim.quote: Significant enhancement of the multiplicities of all observed strange particles relative to negative hadrons was observed in central S+S collisions

name: NA35 enhanced strange-particle production in central sulphur-sulphur collisions

summary.plain: NA35 measured Lambda and K0-short particles in 200 GeV per nucleon sulphur-sulphur and proton-sulphur collisions and saw far more strange particles per negative hadron in central S+S collisions than in p+p or p+S, an early hint of quark-gluon plasma.
summary.technical: Lambda, anti-Lambda and K0s production in the NA35 streamer chamber at 200 GeV/nucleon: the multiplicities of all observed strange particles relative to negative hadrons are significantly enhanced in central S+S collisions compared with p+p and p+S; the Lambda polarisation in central S+S is compatible with zero up to pT = 2 GeV/c.

title: Neutral strange particle production in sulphur-sulphur and proton-sulphur collisions at 200 GeV/nucleon
why_it_matters: Strangeness enhancement was a predicted signature of quark-gluon plasma; the 2026 SPS reviews describe this NA35 result as the first indication of QGP formation at the CERN SPS.
